examples.trans: What happened, did you decide to perk up this morning?

examples.text: Доброе утро!
examples.trans: Good morning!

meanings.note: Prefix 'вз-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'бодриться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to perk up'.

related.gloss: not to to perk up (negated infinitive)

examples.text: А что случилось, решила утром взбодриться?
examples.trans: What happened, did you decide to perk up this morning?

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и взбодриться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to perk up on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Значит, тебе нужно там что-то менять.
examples.trans: Then you need to change something there.

examples.text: Значит, эту записку написал не ты?
examples.trans: So you were not the one who wrote this note?

examples.text: Нужно сначала кого-то на своё место назначить.
examples.trans: First I need to appoint someone in my place.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сейчас это уже не ресторан, а печка.
examples.trans: Right now it is no longer a restaurant, it is a furnace.

examples.text: Ну, это смотря что именно варить.
examples.trans: Well, that depends on what exactly you cook.

examples.text: Это хорошая экономия каждый месяц.
examples.trans: That is a nice savings every month.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'писка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'note' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Значит, эту записку написал не ты?
examples.trans: So you were not the one who wrote this note?

examples.text: Записывай, улица Дорожный проезд.
examples.trans: Write it down, Dorozhny Drive.

examples.text: Никита, признавайся, это твоя записка?
examples.trans: Nikita, admit it, is this your note?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'писать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wrote', paired with 'писать'.

examples.text: Значит, эту записку написал не ты?
examples.trans: So you were not the one who wrote this note?

examples.text: Интересно, и что же в нём написано?
examples.trans: Interesting, and what is written in it?

examples.text: Тут написано, следующую подсказку кормит Сеня.
examples.trans: It says here that Senya feeds the next clue.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нятие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'concept, idea, notion' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Понятия не имею, о чём ты говоришь.
examples.trans: I have no idea what you are talking about.

examples.text: Я вообще без понятия.
examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Понятия не имею.
examples.trans: I have no idea.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to have (formal, in set phrases)'.

examples.text: Ну, это смотря что именно варить.
examples.trans: Well, that depends on what exactly you cook.

examples.text: Понятия не имею, о чём ты говоришь.
examples.trans: I have no idea what you are talking about.

examples.text: Вот именно, официантов я штрафовать не могу.
examples.trans: Exactly, I cannot fine the waiters.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Димочка, ну не расстраивайся ты так.
examples.trans: Dimochka, well do not get so upset.

examples.text: У меня сейчас сплошные нервы и стресс.
examples.trans: I have nothing but nerves and stress right now.

examples.text: Я новый контракт не могу подписать.
examples.trans: I cannot sign a new contract.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'speak', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.text: Ладно, давай мы попозже поговорим.
examples.trans: Alright, let's talk a little later.

examples.text: Понятия не имею, о чём ты говоришь.
examples.trans: I have no idea what you are talking about.

examples.text: Ладно, давай позже поговорим.
examples.trans: Alright, let's talk later.

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'we shall see', paired with 'смотреть'.

examples.text: Можно я посмотрю?
examples.trans: May I have a look?

examples.text: Я только посмотрел.
examples.trans: I only had a look.

examples.text: А можно я пойду посмотрю?
examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will be'.

examples.text: Следуя им, мы оказываемся там, где должны быть.
examples.trans: Following them, we end up where we are meant to be.

examples.text: У меня есть машинка.
examples.trans: I have a toy car.

examples.text: Детство было трудное.
examples.trans: Childhood was hard.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'further, on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ладно, посмотрим, что будет дальше.
examples.trans: Alright, let's see what happens next.

examples.text: Федя, скажи, что мне делать дальше?
examples.trans: Fedya, tell me, what should I do next?

examples.text: Здравствуйте, и что мне делать дальше?
examples.trans: Hello, and what am I supposed to do next?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'later', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ладно, давай мы попозже поговорим.
examples.trans: Alright, let's talk a little later.

examples.text: Ладно, давай позже поговорим.
examples.trans: Alright, let's talk later.

examples.text: Поздравляю, это первый такой ресторан в России!
examples.trans: Congratulations, it is the first such restaurant in Russia!
